title: Linear Equations in Two Variables, Slope, and Linear Functions
lead: These questions share one object: a line in the xy-plane. You will be asked to read a line’s features from its equation or its graph, to write the equation of a line from a few facts, to decide whether a point lies on a line, and to say what a coefficient means in a word problem. The skills transfer between all of them.

parts.title: Part 1 · The core idea
parts.html:
A linear equation in two variables does not have one solution. It has infinitely many: every point (x, y) that satisfies it is a solution, and plotting them all gives a straight line. A line is a picture of an equation, and a point is a solution when it sits on the line.

The same line can be written with function notation. y = 2x − 1 and f(x) = 2x − 1 describe one graph; f(x) is just another name for y.

Three features describe any line: its slope, its y-intercept and its x-intercept.

parts.title: Part 2 · Slope
parts.html:
Slope tells you which way a line goes and how steep it is.

  • A line that rises from left to right has a positive slope.
  • A line that falls from left to right has a negative slope.
  • The steeper the line, the larger the size of the slope. A slope of −5 is steeper than a slope of 2.

Slope is the change in y divided by the change in x, and any two points on the line give the same value:

m=y2−y1x2−x1
A line passes through (−3,2) and (1,14). What is its slope? m=14−21−(−3)=124=3

Keep the order consistent: if 14 comes first on top, its partner 1 comes first on the bottom. Mixing the order flips the sign.

Two special cases:

  • A horizontal line has slope 0. Every point has the same y, so the change in y is 0.
  • A vertical line has an undefined slope. Every point has the same x, so the change in x is 0 and you would be dividing by zero.

In word problems, slope is the per-unit meaning: dollars per ticket, metres per second, pages per day. If a question asks what the slope represents, answer with the units, not the number.

parts.title: Part 3 · Intercepts
parts.html:
The y-intercept is the point where the line crosses the y-axis. Its x-coordinate is always 0. Every line that is not vertical has exactly one.

The x-intercept is the point where the line crosses the x-axis. Its y-coordinate is always 0. Every line that is not horizontal has exactly one.

To find them from an equation, set the other variable to 0. To find them from a graph, read where the line crosses each axis. The two intercepts are also two points, so they give you the slope.

What are the intercepts and the slope of the line shown? y-intercept: (0,4)    x-intercept: (2,0)
m=0−42−0=−42=−2

parts.title: Part 4 · Slope-intercept form
parts.html:
Slope-intercept form is y = mx + b. It shows two features at a glance: m is the slope and b is the y-intercept. The line y = 5x − 2 has slope 5 and crosses the y-axis at −2.

Lines are also written in standard form, Ax + By = C. To read the slope from standard form, solve for y first.

What is the slope of the graph of 2x+5y=20? Subtract 2x from both sides → 5y=−2x+20
Divide both sides by 5 → y=−(25)x+4
Slope −25, y-intercept 4

Common mistake. In standard form Ax + By = C, the slope is −A/B, not A. For 12x + 28y = 2016 the slope is −12/28 = −3/7. Students who see 12 and take it as the slope miss these questions every time.

parts.title: Part 5 · Writing the equation of a line
parts.html:
You can write the equation of a line from either of two sets of facts. In both, the goal is to fill in m and b in y = mx + b.

The slope and one point. You have m, and the point gives you an x and a y. Substitute all three and solve for b.

A line has slope 3 and passes through (2,10). What is its equation? Substitute m=3, x=2, y=10 → 10=3(2)+b
10=6+b → b=4
y=3x+4

If the point you are given is the y-intercept, there is nothing to solve: its y-value is b.

Two points. Find the slope from the two points first, then use either point to find b.

A line passes through (−2,9) and (4,−3). What is its equation? m=−3−94−(−2)=−126=−2
Use (−2,9): 9=−2(−2)+b → 9=4+b → b=5
y=−2x+5
Check with (4,−3): −2(4)+5=−3

Checking with the second point takes a few seconds and confirms both m and b.

parts.title: Part 6 · Parallel and perpendicular lines
parts.html:
Two lines with different slopes cross exactly once. Two slope relationships are special:

  • Parallel lines have the same slope. They never meet, unless they are the same line.
  • Perpendicular lines meet at a 90° angle. Their slopes are negative reciprocals: flip the fraction and change the sign. The negative reciprocal of 1/3 is −3; of −3/7 it is 7/3. The two slopes always multiply to −1.
  • The exception: a vertical line (x = 4, undefined slope) is perpendicular to a horizontal line (y = −2, slope 0). Do not use the reciprocal rule on undefined slopes.

In the graph, lines p and q both have slope 1/2, so they are parallel. Line r (dashed) has slope −2, the negative reciprocal of 1/2, so it is perpendicular to both.

These relationships give you a slope. Add one point and you can write the equation with the method from Part 5.

Line k is parallel to y=4x−1 and passes through (0,7). What is the equation of line k? Parallel → same slope, m=4
(0,7) is the y-intercept → b=7
y=4x+7
A line is perpendicular to y=−2x+3 and meets it at (4,−5). What is its equation? Perpendicular → negative reciprocal of −2 is 12
Substitute m=12, x=4, y=−5 → −5=(12)(4)+b
−5=2+b → b=−7
y=(12)x−7

For questions that only ask whether two lines are parallel or perpendicular, put both in slope-intercept form, or compute −A/B for each, and compare the slopes.

parts.title: Part 7 · Points on a line
parts.html:
“Which point lies on the line?” has one test: plug it in. A point (a, b) is on the line exactly when substituting a for x and b for y makes the equation true. No graphing, no form conversion.

Is (20,60) on 12x+28y=2016? 12(20)+28(60)=240+1680=1920≠2016 → not on the line

The same test answers harder-sounding questions.

The line 3x+ky=15 passes through (2,3). What is k? 3(2)+k(3)=15 → 6+3k=15 → k=3

“A point on the line” is always a substitution in disguise.

parts.title: Part 8 · What the equation means in context
parts.html:
In word problems each piece of Ax + By = C has a meaning. Take 12x + 28y = 2016, where x is standard parcels and y is heavy parcels:

PieceMeaning
12dollars per standard parcel
28dollars per heavy parcel
12x and 28ythe totals from each type
2016the combined total

“How much more does a heavy parcel cost than a standard one?” The answer is 28 − 12 = 16, the difference of the coefficients, not 28y − 12x. The counts x and y do not matter for a per-item comparison.

A question that asks you to interpret 10x in a lumber problem wants “the total boards used for the bookshelves”, not “boards per bookshelf”, which is just 10. Reading the term's role correctly is the whole question.

parts.title: Part 9 · The Desmos workflow
parts.html:
Desmos graphs standard form directly: type 12x+28y=2016 and the line appears. Two high-value uses:

Building a line from two points. When a question gives two points and asks for a y-value elsewhere on the line, enter the points in a table (columns x₁ and y₁), then type y_1~mx_1+b. Desmos fits the exact line. Define f(x)=mx+b and evaluate f(target x). This also solves “find the missing coordinate” questions.

Solving for unknown coefficients. If the line bx + cy = 10 passes through two known points, put the points in a table and enter b x_1 + c y_1 ~ 10. Desmos fits both constants at once. Then substitute the values back into both points to verify, because regression gives decimals that you should convert to exact fractions.

For parallel and perpendicular questions, reasoning by hand is faster than graphing: compute −A/B for each line and compare. The graph is a visual confirmation, not the decision-maker.

parts.title: Part 10 · Things to remember
parts.html:
• Slope: change in y over change in x, m = (y₂ − y₁) / (x₂ − x₁). Horizontal lines have slope 0; vertical lines have an undefined slope.
  • Slope-intercept form: in y = mx + b, m is the slope and b is the y-intercept. Rewrite standard form this way before reading the slope.
  • Writing an equation: you need the slope and one point, or two points.
  • Parallel: same slope. Perpendicular: negative reciprocal slopes.
  • A point is on a line when substituting it makes the equation true.

parts.title: Part 11 · Interpreting the numbers in a model
parts.html:
Many questions give a linear model and ask what one number in it means. Two readings cover most of them: the constant is the value when the variable is 0 (a starting amount), and the coefficient is the change per one unit.

Use the units when it is not obvious. Every term in an equation must be in the same unit as the total.

8a + 5c = 460, where a is the number of adult tickets, c is the number of child tickets, and 460 is the total in dollars. What does 8 represent? The right side is dollars, so 8a must be dollars
a is a number of adult tickets → 8 must be dollars per adult ticket

Check the choice against how the variables are defined. A wrong choice often describes a real rate that the equation does not contain: “per square foot” when the variable is years, or “number sold” when the output is a price.

Change for more than one unit. If the slope is the change per 1 unit, the change per n units is n times the slope.

T(m) = 70 − 4m gives a temperature in degrees after m minutes. By how much does the temperature fall every 6 minutes? Slope −4 → 4 degrees per minute
6×4=24 degrees

The question asked backwards. “How much must x increase for the output to rise by 1?” is the reciprocal of the slope.

h(x) = (3x + 5) / 4 gives a plant's height in centimetres when x grams of fertilizer are used. How many more grams raise the height by exactly 1 cm? Split the fraction → h(x)=(34)x+54 → slope 34 cm per gram
Reciprocal → 43 grams per cm

A line of possible combinations. When a line shows the combinations of two items that use up a fixed budget, each intercept is the number of one item bought with nothing spent on the other.

A $600 budget is spent on chairs and tables. The line of possible combinations crosses the chairs axis at 40. What does one chair cost? 40 chairs and no tables use the whole budget
600÷40=15 → $15
